Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law

appoint verb

to a post or an office

also appointed, nominate, name (to a post), designate, appointment (to a post)

classical

Nep. Them. 2.1: praetor ā populō factus

faciō, facere, fēcī, factum

with two accusatives: aliquem cōnsulem facere; passive fierī, conjugation

make (someone consul, leader): appoint

The plainest way to say who was given a post, whoever gave it. For the people electing, creāre (see election); for putting someone at the head of something, praeficere with the dative (see in charge).

Other words

  • nōminō, nōmināre, nōmināvī, nōminātum — name, nominate (for an office)

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Phil. 2.4: mē augurem … nōmināvērunt; Liv. 1.32 (Lewis & Short)

    To name someone for a post, as the augurs who put forward a new member (Lewis & Short); first of all simply to name, call by name.

  • dēsignō, dēsignāre, dēsignāvī, dēsignātum — appoint in advance, designate

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Sall. C. 26.1: sī dēsignātus foret (Lewis & Short); Cic. Agr. 2.26 (Lewis & Short)

    To mark out, and so to appoint to an office not yet entered: cōnsul dēsignātus, the consul-elect. It also means to point out, describe (Lewis & Short).

  • dīcō, dīcere, dīxī, dictum — appoint (a dictator, a consul): the formal word

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 9.15.2: dictātōrem dīcat (Lewis & Short); Liv. 5.9 (Lewis & Short)

    Used of a magistrate naming a dictator or his master of horse; outside these phrases it means to say.

  • cōnstituō, cōnstituere, cōnstituī, cōnstitūtum — appoint, set up (a guardian, an accuser)

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Div. Caec. 10: accūsātōrem (Lewis & Short); Dig. 2.1.1: tūtōrēs pūpillīs (Lewis & Short)

    To set up, establish: of persons, to put someone forward or appoint him to a role (Lewis & Short); also to decide, fix a day (see establish).

Examples

  • ad quod gerendum praetor ā populō factus

    appointed general by the people to fight itNep. Them. 2.1

  • quō enim tempore mē augurem ā tōtō conlēgiō expetītum Cn. Pompejus et Q. Hortēnsius nōmināvērunt

    for at the time when Pompey and Hortensius nominated me augur, sought by the whole collegeCic. Phil. 2.4

See also election, in charge, position, choose, establish.
